Estimate ECx values from a fitted model

Source: R/ecx.R
ecx.Rd

Estimates the concentration at which the fitted response changes by a given proportion from the control, in each direction, for a fitted concentration-response model.

Usage

ecx(
  object,
  ...,
  proportion = 0.1,
  type = "absolute",
  reference = NULL,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL,
  draws = FALSE,
  prob_vals = c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975),
  xform = identity,
  ecx_val = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  posterior = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  hormesis_def = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  horme = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  by_group = lifecycle::deprecated()
)

Arguments

object

A model fitted with brms, drc or bayesnec, or a toxval_pred object.

...

Additional arguments passed to toxval_predict(), such as n_boot and seed for a drc fit, or asymptote for a brmsfit.

proportion

A numeric vector of effects, as proportions of the span named by type; 0.1 is the EC10. Each value gives its own rows. Not supplied under type = "direct".

type

One of "absolute", "relative", "range" or "direct". See Details.

reference

A number, the response value whose crossing is sought under type = "direct". Supplied only under "direct".

x_var

A string naming the predictor variable in object, or NULL where the class of object records which of its variables is the predictor. Each method states whether it accepts NULL.

group_var

A string naming the grouping variable in object, or NULL for a single curve.

resolution

A whole number giving the number of predictor values to evaluate the curve at. Larger values estimate a metric more precisely.

x_range

A numeric vector of length 2 giving the range of predictor values to evaluate over, or NULL to use the range in the model data. The first value must equal the control concentration.

x_control

A number, the control concentration, at which the control response is predicted and the grid starts, or NULL for the lowest predictor value in the data. A value outside the range of the data warns.

draws

A flag. If TRUE, a draws list column holds the per-realisation values of each row.

prob_vals

A numeric vector of the central, lower and upper quantiles to summarise the realisations by, in that order.

xform

A function applied to the per-realisation concentrations before they are summarised, such as exp for a model fitted on log concentration. It must be monotone over the evaluated range and may be decreasing.

ecx_val

Use proportion, or reference under type = "direct".

posterior

Supplying it is an error. Use draws.

hormesis_def, horme

Both directions are now always estimated, so these are ignored.

by_group

Supplying group_var gives one estimate per level.

Value

A toxval tibble with one row per curve, proportion and direction, and the columns:

  • metric: "ecx".

  • direction: "decreasing" or "increasing".

  • group: the level of group_var, where it is supplied.

  • response: the response of a multivariate fit.

  • estimate, conf.low, conf.high: the ECx, as the prob_vals quantiles of the realisations, after xform.

  • proportion, type: the arguments of the call. proportion is NA under type = "direct".

  • control: the predicted response at the control concentration, or NA under type = "direct".

  • reference: the response whose crossing is the ECx.

  • asymptote: the asymptote the span is measured to, or NA unless type is "relative".

  • draws: where draws = TRUE, a tibble per row of .draw and value.draw, the ECx of each realisation, after xform. A realisation that does not reach the reference is Inf, or -Inf where xform is decreasing, and one excluded from the summary is NA.

control, reference and asymptote are on the response scale, as the central prob_vals quantile of the realisations. The tibble prints the model class and the number of realisations above the rows.

Details

The model is evaluated over a grid of concentrations once per realisation, by toxval_predict(): once per posterior draw for a Bayesian fit, and once per parametric bootstrap replicate for a frequentist one. The ECx is found for each realisation and the realisations are summarised by prob_vals.

Each realisation is searched for both a decreasing and an increasing crossing, and each direction is a row of the result. A direction in which no realisation crosses is returned with NA estimates.

type names what proportion is taken of, from the control, the predicted response at the control concentration, by default the lowest concentration in the data (see toxval_predict()):

  • "absolute" (the default): decreasing, the control down to 0; increasing, the control up to 1 for a response on the proportion scale, and otherwise up to twice the control.

  • "relative": the control to the lower (decreasing) or upper (increasing) asymptote of the curve, a parameter of the fitted equation. It is available where the fit supplies the asymptote: from the limits of a drc fit, and for a brmsfit from the parameters named by asymptote (see toxval_predict()). An asymptote outside the observed responses is an extrapolation, and relative inherits its uncertainty. Before toxval 2.0.0 "relative" meant what is now "range", so supplying it warns.

  • "range": the control to the lowest (decreasing) or highest (increasing) response the curve predicts.

  • "direct": no proportion; the ECx is where the curve crosses the response value supplied as reference.

A realisation that does not reach the reference within the evaluated range ranks above the highest concentration, and an interval limit that falls among such realisations is reported as the highest concentration, with a warning. When any realisation is censored, the reported quantiles are observed order statistics. Under "range" this includes a realisation that never falls below, or rises above, its control. Under "absolute" and "relative", a realisation with nothing to take the proportion of, such as a control at or below 0 or a missing asymptote, is excluded from the summary, with a warning.

Fits from bayesnec

ecx() also accepts a bayesnecfit or bayesmanecfit from bayesnec::bnec() when bayesnec is installed. bayesnec has its own ecx(), and when both packages are loaded with library(), the one loaded last is used. Call toxval::ecx() to make sure this function runs. The two functions can give different estimates for the same fit, because they evaluate the curve at different concentrations.

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- drc::drm(rootl ~ conc, data = drc::ryegrass, fct = drc::LL.4())

# EC10 and EC50, as proportions of the span from the control down to 0
ecx(fit, proportion = c(0.1, 0.5), seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 10
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  estimate conf.low conf.high proportion type     control
#>   <chr>  <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 ecx    decreasing     1.48     1.03      1.87        0.1 absolute    7.80
#> 2 ecx    increasing    NA       NA        NA           0.1 absolute    7.80
#> 3 ecx    decreasing     3.19     2.87      3.55        0.5 absolute    7.80
#> 4 ecx    increasing    NA       NA        NA           0.5 absolute    7.80
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>

# EC10 of the span from the control to the lower asymptote
ecx(fit, type = "relative", seed = 42)
#> Warning: `type = "relative"` now measures from the control to the asymptote of the curve. Before toxval 2.0.0 it measured to the extent of the curve, which is now `type = "range"`; the two also differ for a non-monotonic curve, because `range` measures from the control rather than from the maximum.
#> Warning: Some realisations have no crossing within the evaluated range, so a reported quantile is at the highest concentration, or have no reference and were excluded. Consider a wider `x_range`.
#> * increasing: 100.0% excluded
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  estimate conf.low conf.high proportion type     control
#>   <chr>  <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 ecx    decreasing     1.45     1.01      1.82        0.1 relative    7.80
#> 2 ecx    increasing    NA       NA        NA           0.1 relative   NA   
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>

# EC10 of the span from the control to the lowest predicted response
ecx(fit, type = "range", seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  estimate conf.low conf.high proportion type  control
#>   <chr>  <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>   <dbl>
#> 1 ecx    decreasing     1.45     1.00      1.82        0.1 range    7.80
#> 2 ecx    increasing    NA       NA        NA           0.1 range    7.80
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>

# concentration at which the predicted root length falls to 4
ecx(fit, type = "direct", reference = 4, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  estimate conf.low conf.high proportion type   control
#>   <chr>  <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>    <dbl>
#> 1 ecx    decreasing     3.13     2.85      3.45         NA direct      NA
#> 2 ecx    increasing    NA       NA        NA            NA direct      NA
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>

# per-realisation values of each row
res <- ecx(fit, draws = TRUE, seed = 42)
res$draws[[1]]
#> # A tibble: 1,000 × 2
#>    .draw value.draw
#>    <int>      <dbl>
#>  1     1       1.76
#>  2     2       1.51
#>  3     3       1.93
#>  4     4       1.27
#>  5     5       1.72
#>  6     6       1.59
#>  7     7       1.65
#>  8     8       1.63
#>  9     9       1.53
#> 10    10       1.46
#> # ℹ 990 more rows

# one estimate per herbicide
fit_group <- drc::drm(
  DryMatter ~ Dose,
  curveid = Herbicide,
  data = drc::S.alba,
  fct = drc::LL.4()
)
ecx(fit_group, group_var = "Herbicide", seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 11
#> # Model:    drc
#> # Settings: resolution 500 | 1000 bootstrap realisations
#>   metric direction  group   estimate conf.low conf.high proportion type  control
#>   <chr>  <chr>      <fct>      <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>   <dbl>
#> 1 ecx    decreasing Bentaz…     19.6     13.9      24.7        0.1 abso…    3.81
#> 2 ecx    increasing Bentaz…     NA       NA        NA          0.1 abso…    3.81
#> 3 ecx    decreasing Glypho…     30.1     12.2      41.1        0.1 abso…    3.88
#> 4 ecx    increasing Glypho…     NA       NA        NA          0.1 abso…    3.88
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: reference <dbl>, asymptote <dbl>
# }
